prompt: Authentic consumer dashcam footage, recorded through a windscreen from the driver's eye height. Fixed wide-angle lens, everything in focus, no camera moves and no zoom. Flat unedited colour, mild video compression, slight engine vibration. Overcast even daylight, no lens flare, no shallow depth of field, no colour grading. The car holds a steady lane at normal traffic speed. The car is driving on a wide three-lane interstate highway with a concrete median barrier. Ahead on the road in the car's own lane, about a hundred metres away, is a torn scrap of black rubber, roughly 40 centimetres long, lying completely flat on the asphalt and barely raised off the road surface, in the left-hand lane. Shed tire tread in the left travel lane, partially in the shadow of the overpass. It is visible but unremarkable, small at first and growing only as the car gets nearer, the way a real object does. The car approaches at a steady speed and continues past it without stopping. Throughout the shot it keeps exactly the same size and shape, and stays flat against the road surface, small enough that it covers only a narrow part of one lane and never rises higher than the kerb.
